global._doc_wg_bind_ip: Caddy's wg0 IP on gcp-proxy (10.0.0.1) — every public *.diegonmarcos.com site block dual-binds to (0.0.0.0, wg_bind_ip). Caddy lives on gcp-proxy (the public-facing VM); reverse-proxy upstreams to internal services traverse the wg0 mesh (10.0.0.x). Engine resolveVmIpForCaddy() still prefers wg-public IPs (10.1.0.x) when both endpoints are peers — gcp-proxy is a wg-public peer (10.1.0.2) so mail-side upstreams keep using wg-public transit.
global._doc_wg_cidrs: Source CIDRs that count as "on the mesh" for every wg_only / bearer gate caddyfile.nix emits (@wg, @not_wg). Mirrors config.json wireguard.subnet + wireguard.subnet_v6. The wg0 mesh went dual-stack on 2026-07-26 but this gate stayed IPv4-only, so any client resolving the AAAA record (fd0c:1d00::1 — Hickory serves both, and clients prefer IPv6) arrived from fd0c:1d00::/64, missed the matcher and got 403. Keep both families listed or mesh-only routes break for IPv6-capable peers. Space-separated: Caddy remote_ip takes a CIDR list.

edge_auth._doc: THE edge auth policy, one list, three tiers. Every public URL is exactly one of: (a) private -- mesh/WireGuard only (route wg_only:true, or a *.app/.db/s3 name), answered 403 to any non-mesh source and never served by the public edge (caddy-public); (b) public-protected -- the DEFAULT for anything public: the shared (edge_auth) snippet requires `Authorization: Bearer <fleet token>` (introspect-proxy) OR a valid Authelia session cookie, else 401 (API / non-browser) or 302 to auth. (browser); (c) public-open -- anonymous allowed, ONLY what is listed in public_open / technical below, each with a reason. Adding a host to public_open is the only way to make something anonymous; add more entries here. The CI guard (cloud-infra 9_others/test/edge-auth-gate.test.sh) fails on a public site that is in no tier, in two tiers, or open without an entry here. Rendered by _shared/edge-auth.nix into BOTH Caddyfiles (hub infra-sec_caddy, edge infra-sec_caddy-public); the derive copies this block into build-caddy.json and build-caddy-edge.json.

public_open.reason: The IdP itself: login portal and OIDC endpoints (authorize / token / JWKS / discovery) cannot require the token or session they exist to issue.
Owner decision 2026-10-16: the public link page is deliberately anonymous.
Owner decision 2026-10-16: MCP OAuth discovery metadata (RFC 9728 / RFC 8414) is read by a client BEFORE it holds a token. Only these two documents; every MCP endpoint stays Bearer-protected.

Owner decision 2026-10-16: the tracker script and its event-collection endpoint are loaded by anonymous visitors of the public websites (umami script.js + /api/send; Matomo's tracker equivalents). Dashboards, the reporting APIs (matomo api.php, umami /api/*) and OpenObserve stay protected.
Owner decision 2026-10-16: other homeservers federate and discover this one without credentials. Client API (/_matrix/client/*, media) stays protected.

Owner decision 2026-10-16: the wstunnel client opens a WebSocket upgrade to a secret path prefix and cannot do a cookie/bearer handshake. The exemption is `Upgrade: websocket` only; wstunnel itself rejects every upgrade whose path is not its secret --http-upgrade-path-prefix, and every non-upgrade request to vpn. is gated.

technical.reason: Owner decision 2026-10-16: ACME http-01 validation requests come from the CA and cannot carry a token. Exempted on EVERY host (the path is excluded from the gate). Caddy core answers a live token before any route runs; this fleet itself issues via DNS-01.

Browsers never attach credentials to a CORS preflight. The (edge_auth) snippet answers it itself with 204; it is never proxied to an upstream, so it serves no content. Plain OPTIONS (WebDAV discovery) is NOT exempt.
IMAPS / SMTPS are not HTTP: caddy-l4 forwards the raw TLS stream to Stalwart, which authenticates the mail login itself. There is no HTTP request to carry a bearer or cookie.

catch_all._redirect_doc: Unknown subdomains 302 to the landing hub instead of the 404 error page (caddyfile.nix catchAllBlock). page stays as the edge's fallback file.

mail_l4_routes.comment: IMAPS via SNI on :443 -> STALWART :2993 (2026-09-02). Maddy :993 (go-imap v1) advertises no CONDSTORE/QRESYNC/UIDPLUS, which forces clients into a full flag rescan of every synced folder each poll -- measured on-device: 9355 UID FLAGS fetches per 15-min pass, all night, phone dead at 04:49. Stalwart :2993 advertises CONDSTORE+QRESYNC+UIDPLUS+IMAP4rev2. The earlier objection to :2993 (IMAP clients see Stalwart's ENTIRE 1*-9* + A*-F* tree because JMAP and IMAP share one store) is mitigated by the subscription policy in mail-rules-profile-diego.json folder_options: only INBOX + the F* sender folders are subscribed, and clients honouring LSUB/subscriptions see the intended menu. Maddy keeps :25 inbound and its store stays intact for rollback: revert this upstream to oci-mail:993.
SMTPS via SNI on :443 → Stalwart :2465 (Maddy's :465 is legacy)

identity._doc: Which gitea user each identity the edge validated acts as (gitea reverse-proxy authentication). `bearer` is keyed by the fleet client_id introspect-proxy returns in X-Auth-User; `session` by the Authelia username forward_auth returns in Remote-User — the cloud-drive app reaches gitea with the Authelia session cookie, never a bearer, so without that row the phone could not see a private repo. The hub caddy strips any inbound `header` before forward_auth, sets it only from these tables, and answers 403 for a validated identity that has no row: an unmapped client never falls through to anonymous or to a default user. `diego` is the only human gitea account and owns every repo. Add a row here, not anywhere else.
